12377-the-court-of-boyville.title: The Court Of Boyville
12377-the-court-of-boyville.creator: William Allen White
12377-the-court-of-boyville.description: A book by William Allen White. We who are passing "through the wilderness of this world" find it difficult to realize what an impenetrable wall there is around the town of Boyville. Storm it as we may with the simulation of light-heartedness, bombard it with our heavy guns, loaded with fishing-hooks and golf-sticks, and skates and base-balls, and butterfly-nets, the walls remain.

32039-the-third-day-at-stone-s-river.title: The Third Day At Stone S River
32039-the-third-day-at-stone-s-river.creator: Unknown
32039-the-third-day-at-stone-s-river.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. a battery of artillery, moved over towards the Nashville pike and turned his attention to the immense supply train of the army. A portion of this train, six miles long when stretched out upon the road, was moving across the country from the Wilkinson to the Nashville pike. The scene was one of the most indescribable confusion.

arxiv-2104-01290.title: Measuring Linguistic Diversity During COVID-19
arxiv-2104-01290.creator: Jonathan Dunn, Tom Coupe, Benjamin Adams
arxiv-2104-01290.description: Abstract Computational measures of linguistic diversity help us understand the linguistic landscape using digital language data. The contribution of this paper is to calibrate measures of linguistic diversity using restrictions on international travel resulting from the COVID-19 pandemic. Previous work has mapped the distribution of languages using geo-referenced social media and web data.

arxiv-2109-14099.title: An Explainable AI Approach for Diagnosis of COVID-19 using MALDI-ToF Mass Spectrometry
arxiv-2109-14099.creator: Venkata Devesh Reddy Seethi, Zane LaCasse, Prajkta Chivte, Joshua Bland, Shrihari S. Kadkol, Elizabeth R. Gaillard, Pratool Bharti, Hamed Alhoori
arxiv-2109-14099.description: Abstract The severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus type- 2 2 (SARS‐CoV‐ 2 2 ) caused a global pandemic and immensely affected the global economy. Accurate, cost-effective, and quick tests have proven substantial in identifying infected people and mitigating the spread.

We compute the principal specialization of the skew Schur polynomials s λ / μ ​ ( x 1 , … , x k ) s_{\lambda/\mu}(x_{1},\ldots,x_{k}) modulo q m − 1 q^{m}-1 under suitable conditions.

arxiv-2203-11048.title: How Do We Answer Complex Questions: Discourse Structure of Long-form Answers
arxiv-2203-11048.creator: Fangyuan Xu Junyi Jessy Li Eunsol Choi
arxiv-2203-11048.description: Abstract Long-form answers, consisting of multiple sentences, can provide nuanced and comprehensive answers to a broader set of questions. To better understand this complex and understudied task, we study the functional structure of long-form answers collected from three datasets, ELI5 Fan et al. 2019 , WebGPT Nakano et al. 2021 and Natural Questions Kwiatkowski et al. 2019 .

arxiv-2306-15116.title: Streaming quantum gate set tomography using the extended Kalman filter
arxiv-2306-15116.creator: J. P. Marceaux, Kevin Young
arxiv-2306-15116.description: Abstract Closed-loop control algorithms for real-time calibration of quantum processors require efficient filters that can estimate physical error parameters based on streams of measured quantum circuit outcomes. Development of such filters is complicated by the highly nonlinear relationship relationship between observed circuit outcomes and the magnitudes of elementary errors.

arxiv-2409-10692.title: Encoding Reusable Multi-Robot Planning Strategies as Abstract Hypergraphs
arxiv-2409-10692.creator: Khen Elimelech, James Motes, Marco Morales, Nancy M. Amato, Moshe Y. Vardi, Lydia E. Kavraki
arxiv-2409-10692.description: Abstract Multi-Robot Task Planning (MR-TP) is the search for a discrete-action plan a team of robots should take to complete a task. The complexity of such problems scales exponentially with the number of robots and task complexity, making them challenging for online solution.

arxiv-2511-12814.title: Quantifying and minimizing dissipation in a non-equilibrium phase transition
arxiv-2511-12814.creator: Yuejun Shen, Zhiqiao Jiang, Yunfan Huang, Brittany M. Cleary, Yixing Jiang, Grant M. Rotskoff, Aaron M. Lindenberg
arxiv-2511-12814.description: Abstract In a finite-time continuous phase transition, topological defects emerge as the system undergoes spontaneous symmetry breaking. The Kibble-Zurek mechanism predicts how the defect density scales with the quench rate. During such processes, dissipation also arises as the system fails to adiabatically follow the control protocol near the critical point.

arxiv-2512-16620.title: Plug to Place: Indoor Multimedia Geolocation from Electrical Sockets for Digital Investigation Journal: DFRWS EU 2026
arxiv-2512-16620.creator: Kanwal Aftab, Graham Adams, Mark Scanlon
arxiv-2512-16620.description: Abstract Computer vision is a rapidly evolving field, giving rise to powerful new tools and techniques in digital forensic investigation, and shows great promise for novel digital forensic applications. One such application, indoor multimedia geolocation, has the potential to become a crucial aid for law enforcement in the fight against human trafficking, child exploitation, and other serious crimes.

arxiv-2512-17128.title: Hermitian Hulls of Rational Algebraic Geometry Codes and Applications in Quantum Codes
arxiv-2512-17128.creator: Lin Sok, Martianus Frederic Ezerman, San Ling
arxiv-2512-17128.description: Abstract Interest in the hulls of linear codes has been growing rapidly. More is known when the inner product is Euclidean than Hermitian. A shift to the latter is gaining traction. The focus is on a code whose Hermitian hull dimension and dual distance can be systematically determined.

Endoplasmic reticulum (ER) stress elicits the unfolded protein response (UPR), initially aimed at coping with the stress, but triggering cell death upon further stress. pmc-10706916.title: Epidemiological and Clinical Characteristics of Adult and Pediatric Patients with Chronic Spontaneous Urticaria
pmc-10706916.creator: Aviv Barzilai, Alona Baum, Moshe Ben-Shoshan, Ido Tzanani, Reman Hakroush, Dan Coster, Michal Solomon, Shoshana Greenberger, Miles Weinberger, Stamatis Gregoriou
pmc-10706916.description: Chronic spontaneous urticaria (CSU) is when lesions occur for ≥6 weeks. However, its underlying mechanism remains unclear. CSU prevalence is similar in adult and pediatric patients; nevertheless, few data are available on CSU characteristics in pediatric patients. We aimed to describe the epidemiology, clinical features, and treatment approach of CSU in pediatrics and adults.

pmc-11280228.title: High Global Health Security Index is a determinant of early detection and response to monkeypox: A cross-sectional study
pmc-11280228.creator: Max Carlos Ramírez-Soto, Hugo Arroyo-Hernández, Moises Leon Juarez, Moises Leon Juarez, Moises Leon Juarez
pmc-11280228.description: IntroductionRecent outbreaks of monkeypox (Mpox) have occurred in countries outside of Africa, with large numbers of cases spreading rapidly to almost every continent. We aimed to analyze the correlation between the Global Health Security (GHS) Index (categories and indicators) and the Mpox case rate in different regions and globally.

pmc-11422046.title: Hyperspectral reflectance imaging for visualizing reducing sugar content, moisture, and hollow rate in red ginseng
pmc-11422046.creator: Xueyuan Bai, Yuting You, Hairui Wang, Daqing Zhao, Jiawen Wang, Wei Zhang
pmc-11422046.description: Red ginseng (RG) has been traditionally valued in Northeast Asia for its health-enhancing properties. Recent advancements in hyperspectral imaging (HSI) offer a non-destructive, efficient, and reliable method to assess critical quality indicators of RG, such as reducing sugar content (RSC), water content (WC), and hollow rate (HR).

pmc-11431491.title: The Many Roles of Precision in Action
pmc-11431491.creator: Jakub Limanowski, Rick A. Adams, James Kilner, Thomas Parr
pmc-11431491.description: Active inference describes (Bayes-optimal) behaviour as being motivated by the minimisation of surprise of one’s sensory observations, through the optimisation of a generative model (of the hidden causes of one’s sensory data) in the brain. One of active inference’s key appeals is its conceptualisation of precision as biasing neuronal communication and, thus, inference within generative models.

pmc-11548485.title: A Federated Reinforcement Learning Framework via a Committee Mechanism for Resource Management in 5G Networks
pmc-11548485.creator: Jaewon Jeong, Joohyung Lee
pmc-11548485.description: This paper proposes a novel decentralized federated reinforcement learning (DFRL) framework that integrates deep reinforcement learning (DRL) with decentralized federated learning (DFL). The DFRL framework boosts efficient virtual instance scaling in Mobile Edge Computing (MEC) environments for 5G core network automation. It enables multiple MECs to collaboratively optimize resource allocation without centralized data sharing.

pmc-11643795.title: Synthesis, Characterization and Catalytic/Antimicrobial Activities of Some Transition Metal Complexes Derived from 2-Floro-N-((2-Hydroxyphenyl)Methylene)Benzohydrazide
pmc-11643795.creator: Ahmed K. Hijazi, Ziyad A. Taha, Dua’a K. Issa, Heba M. Alshare, Waleed M. Al-Momani, Ali Elrashidi, Ahmad S. Barham
pmc-11643795.description: Background: In the last few decades, the field of coordination chemistry has grown very fast, especially in the fields of pharmaceutical, biological and catalytic studies. In ancient times, metals were thought to be beneficial to health issues but nowadays the link between organic–metal substances and different industrial and medicinal properties is well established.

pmc-12553024.title: Topological segmentation of mass spectrometry imaging data
pmc-12553024.creator: Maria M Derkach, Anatoly A Sorokin, Andrey A Kuzin, Eugene N Nikolaev, Igor A Popov, Stanislav I Pekov
pmc-12553024.description:
A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Graphical abstractKeywords: Mass spectrometry, Data analysis, Segmentation, Cosine similarity, Mass spectrometry imaging

Introduction

Mass spectrometry imaging (MSI) is a powerful tool for spatial omics research, applicable to a wide range of biological and biomedical questions. With the advancement of high-spatial-resolution ionisation techniques, MSI is increasingly employed to investigate tissue molecular composition at the cellular level [[1], [2], [3], [4], [5], [6]].

pmc-12607590.title: Recent Advances Towards Selenium Nanoparticles: Synthetic Methods, Functional Mechanisms, and Biological Applications
pmc-12607590.creator: Lulu Geng, Linling Li, Xuening Sun, Shuiyuan Cheng, Jiangling He
pmc-12607590.description: The exceptional physicochemical properties of selenium nanoparticles (SeNPs) have led to their widespread development. The function of SeNPs is significantly influenced by their shape and particle size, which are in turn determined by the applied synthesis methods. This work presents a critical and comparative analysis of physical, chemical, and biosynthetic methods.

pmc-12717189.title: Poly(acrylamide/styrenesulfonic acid) hydrogels for effective removal of Cr(III) ions
pmc-12717189.creator: Abdalla M Khedr, Ashraf A Lotfalla, Kazuhiro Hara, Satoru Yoshioka, Mohamed Gaber
pmc-12717189.description: Techniques for chromium ion removal have been researched more and more because of the significant harm to human health posed by this hazardous contamination in water. The present work represents the preparation of poly[acrylamide(Acr)/styrenesulfonicacid sodium salt (Sty)] hydrogels by free radical cross-linking polymerization applying various Acr and Sty monomer molar ratios.

pmc-13151081.title: A scoping review of guides and advice for scholarly citing in health research
pmc-13151081.creator: Lasse Østengaard, Tine Tjørnhøj-Thomsen, Asger S. Paludan-Müller, Mia Elkjær, Tove Faber Frandsen, Asbjørn Hróbjartsson
pmc-13151081.description: ObjectivesTo identify, summarise and analyse documents with guides and advice for scholarly citing in health research.MethodsIn a scoping review, we included documents with guides and advice for scholarly citing in health research. We searched in Embase (Ovid), Google Scholar, 20 textbooks, 30 journal websites, and conducted supplementary searches.

pmc-13437183.description: What is already known about this topic?Human infections with influenza A(H1N2)v viruses of swine origin have been sporadically reported in several countries, usually following direct or indirect exposure to pigs or contaminated environments. However, sustained human-to-human transmission has not yet been documented.What is added by this report?

pmc-13458584.title: Tropical rivers face severe oxygen stress caused by heat and organic matter: new evidence by stable isotopes
pmc-13458584.creator: Sachintha Senarathne, Robert van Geldern, Rohana Chandrajith, Johannes A C Barth
pmc-13458584.description: Many rivers worldwide exhibit declining dissolved oxygen (DO) concentrations due to changes in hydroclimatic conditions and land use. Our study shows a typical tropical river in Sri Lanka (the Deduru Oya) with DO concentrations between 1.5 and 9.7 mg L−1. In this dataset, almost 80% of all collected water samples were undersaturated.

pmc-13642170.title: LaZeTrack: An open‐source object detection algorithm to detect and track 2‐day‐old zebrafish motor touch responses
pmc-13642170.creator: Adrien Lacroix, Gary Alan Barclay Armstrong
pmc-13642170.description: Zebrafish are a model organism used for the study of vertebrate development, disease, and drug discovery. Two‐day old zebrafish exhibit burst swimming behavior that can be elicited by a light touch to the tail. Motor touch responses are frequently video‐recorded and later analyzed by hand.
